question: This diagram shows a synthetic brain connectivity network. Each circle is a neural region. Each arrow is a one-way connection: a signal can only travel along it in the direction of the arrowhead. Where two regions are joined by two curved arrows, these are two separate one-way connections. Each connection is labelled with its conduction delay in milliseconds. A signal travels from the sensory input region MT (marked IN) to the motor output region Cb (marked OUT) along the route with the smallest total delay. Four connections are marked A, B, C and D. Exactly one of them can be removed on its own without increasing the smallest total delay from MT to Cb. Which one? Answer with a single letter.
references: Dijkstra EW. A note on two problems in connexion with graphs. Numer Math. 1959;1:269-271
Sporns O. Networks of the Brain. MIT Press, 2010 (modular, redundant connectivity)

question: This diagram shows a synthetic brain connectivity network. Each circle is a neural region. Each line is a bidirectional connection. Each connection is labelled with its conduction delay in milliseconds. A signal travels from the sensory input region V1 (marked IN) to the motor output region BG (marked OUT) along the route with the smallest total delay. The two connections marked X and Y both fail at the same time and can no longer carry any signal. After both failures, what is the smallest total delay in milliseconds from V1 to BG? Answer with a whole number.
references: Dijkstra EW. A note on two problems in connexion with graphs. Numer Math. 1959;1:269-271
Sporns O. Networks of the Brain. MIT Press, 2010 (modular, redundant connectivity)

question: This diagram shows a synthetic brain connectivity network. Each circle is a neural region. Connections ending in an arrowhead are excitatory and carry the signal in the direction of the arrowhead. Connections ending in a flat bar are inhibitory and cannot carry the signal. The grey hatched region marked LESION is damaged: no signal can enter or pass through it. Each connection is labelled with its conduction delay in milliseconds. Every region the signal passes through between IN and OUT also adds its own processing delay, shown inside its circle. A signal travels from the sensory input region S2 (marked IN) to the motor output region M1 (marked OUT) along the route with the smallest total delay. The two connections marked X and Y both fail at the same time and can no longer carry any signal. After both failures, what is the smallest total delay in milliseconds from S2 to M1? Answer with a whole number.
references: Dijkstra EW. A note on two problems in connexion with graphs. Numer Math. 1959;1:269-271
Sporns O. Networks of the Brain. MIT Press, 2010 (modular, redundant connectivity)
Inhibitory connections drawn with a flat bar end, excitatory with an arrowhead: standard circuit-diagram notation
